name: Pitch journalists, send media releases and track coverage
summary: Pitches journalists, sends media releases and tracks replies to each pitch, through the agency's Gmail. Crons draft each pitch and follow-up, check threads for replies, and draft one joined report to the owner. A person approves every send. Published coverage is not tracked yet.

all.evidence: 1 discovery call describes this way of doing PR: an agency pitches the business to publications and sends results to the owner

covered_by.media-list: settings (a list the owner or agency approves; no media database is mapped)
covered_by.send-release: approval (the pitch is the release text)

crons.name: pitch
crons.summary: Draft one pitch to each approved journalist who has not had one, and queue each send for approval.

crons.name: follow-up
crons.summary: Mark approved pitches as sent, stop the chase on any reply, and queue the follow-ups that are due (22:00 UTC is 8 am in eastern Australia).

crons.name: report
crons.summary: Weekly: draft one joined report of pitches, replies and follow-ups to the owner, and queue it for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: a Gmail draft that a person can edit, and a read of a pitch thread. Sending a draft is a live operation and waits for a person.

google-workspace.covers: Gmail: draft each pitch, follow-up and report, check a pitch thread for a reply, send the draft after approval

gaps: Cision and Meltwater: their help pages name media lists, pitching, Smart Alerts and reporting, but the kit maps no operations for them (no platform folder). Media lists, story spotting and coverage alerts stay manual until those platforms are mapped.
Published coverage (articles, mentions, share of voice) is not tracked. The report shows replies in the pitch thread only, because no mapped platform reads published coverage.
Results are not tied to bookings or revenue. Nothing in the call evidence or the kit links a placement to a booking.
Journalist lists come from settings that a person writes. There is no media database step.
Writing the release and each pitch, and choosing who to pitch, is judgment work for the agent skill. The cron sends only the release text it is given.
Google Workspace is docs-only: its platform status is spec and it is tested offline. A live Workspace account has to prove the draft, thread-read and send calls.
Reply detection looks only in the sending mailbox. A reply that lands in another mailbox is not seen, so the chase may run once more than it should.

evidence.calls: 1 call in the worklist (all-pr-media); it describes an agency pitching and reporting results, with no tool named
evidence.platforms: Cision, Meltwater and Google Workspace help pages mapped by step. Only Google Workspace has operations in the kit (Gmail drafts, threads and sends); Cision and Meltwater have none
